pulls.title: Initial content: SLH-DSA-FEW (SP 800-230) for X.509
pulls.author: fluppe2
pulls.body:
First full draft text, merging two sources:

- RFC 9909 (FelixKnopp/x509-slhdsa@b3b216f) as the base
- Felix's draft on branch `add-slh-dsa-24-parameter-sets` (FelixKnopp/x509-slhdsa@811cd19)

## Contents
- Pure and HashSLH-DSA-FEW OIDs (`TBD1`–`TBD12`, to be assigned by NIST), in SP 800-230 order
- "Use in X.509" section referring to RFC 9909 Sections 4–7
- Operational and security considerations for the 2^24 signature limit: signature counting across HSMs/replicas, CA/CRL/OCSP, keys that sign on demand (TLS, OCSP) SHOULD use FIPS 205 parameter sets
- Complete ASN.1 module (`asn1/X509-SLHDSA-FEW-2026.asn`) including `SignatureAlgorithms`, `SMimeCaps`, `PublicKeyAlgorithms`; module OID requested in the SMI PKIX module registry
- Authors: Kaveh Bashiri, Felix Knopp, Stavros Kousidis
- `CODEOWNERS` for `@spec-workbench/slhdsa-fewsigs-editors`, placeholder `examples/`

## Changes compared to Felix's branch, please review
- Removed the claim that security "does not degrade gradually" beyond the limit; replaced it with "no longer guaranteed" plus an editor's note. Please check against KP22 / SP 800-230.
- Reworded "signatures generated beyond the limit are indistinguishable from valid ones" to refer to forgeries.
- Fixed the ASN.1 module (`# Todo` line, module OID arc, missing `SignatureAlgorithms`/`SMimeCaps` sets, set name `PublicKeyAlgorithms`).
- IANA: standard request in "SMI Security for PKIX Module Identifier" instead of "to be determined".

## Open issues (editor's notes in the draft)
- OIDs from NIST CSOR
- Re-check against the final SP 800-230
- HashSLH-DSA-FEW: needed? NIST OIDs?
- CMS in this document or a separate one?

Builds cleanly; `make idnits` shows no errors (remaining warnings: RFC 5912 downref, which is in the downref registry, and `<CODE BEGINS>`, both as in RFC 9909).
